header: Date: 2025-05-07 | Time: 09:23 AM PDT | Duration: 55m | Attendees: Avery Kim (Redwood AE), Marcus Li (Redwood SE), Leah Ortiz (Redwood CSM), Sofia Martinez (Greenline), Ethan Cole (Greenline), Priya Nair (Greenline), Ravi Shah (Greenline)
summary: Weekly POC sync to review benchmark results versus Greenline's baseline provider. Discussed throughput and tail-latency (p95/p99) differences, impact of batching and KV cache, quantization tradeoffs, and Dedicated vs Hosted deployment paths. Agreed on follow-ups: run additional p99 tests with KV cache, share updated spreadsheets and logs, schedule on-site Dedicated run, and send pricing and security docs.
topics: Benchmark summary; latency (p50/p95/p99) and throughput (tokens/sec, reqs/sec) comparison vs baseline; KV cache and prefix caching effect; batching strategy; quantization profile (4-bit vs 8-bit) impact; Dedicated cluster sizing; next steps and action items.
transcript:
[00:00] Avery (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we can start. Uh, good to see you all. This is the weekly POC sync to go over the benchmark numbers vs your baseline provider. Marcus is with me, our SE, and Leah from CS. Sofia, Priya, Ethan - you there?

[00:12] Sofia (Greenline): Yep, here. Thanks, Avery. We pulled in the latest spreadsheet you sent yesterday, so we'll jump straight to the numbers.

[00:22] Marcus (Redwood SE): Great. Quick agenda: I'll run through the runs we did last week on the r-model variant, compare to the baseline runs you shared, highlight where tail latency differs, then we can talk tuning knobs - batching, cache, quantization - and propose next steps.

[01:05] Ethan: Quick note, our baseline provider is BaselineCloudAI, they're running a 16GB GPU config, single-tenant. Our goal is p95 < 250ms and p99 < 500ms on that prompt mix at 60 concurrent users.

[01:20] Marcus: Thanks. Okay, slide or sheet 1 - throughput. Redwood median tokens/sec: about 2300 tokens/sec for the r-model-13b quant-8 run at 8 concurrent workers; baseline reported ~1800 tokens/sec for their 16GB instance. So throughput improved about ~28%. But the important bit is tail latency...

[02:05] Sofia: We saw higher p99 on Redwood in one of the runs; can you explain that?

[02:12] Marcus: Yeah, we expected that to show up raw. Two main factors: first, some runs were cold (no KV cache warmup), and second, batching settings hit spikes in queueing under bursty load. Example p99 numbers: Redwood hosted (no cache, batch size auto) p95=210ms, p99=610ms; Baseline p95=240ms, p99=430ms. So p95 is better on Redwood, p99 initially worse.

[03:01] Priya: That p99 delta is the one that worries us. Our SLO clipping is strict. What do you recommend?

[03:08] Marcus: Two immediate levers - enable KV prefix cache for your common prompts and adjust max batch delay to reduce queuing spikes. When we re-ran with KV cache warmed and conservative batch_delay (5ms cap) we got p95=220ms, p99=380ms on Redwood - so p99 improved past baseline.

[03:45] Ravi: Can you show the p99 run logs? We need to see request traces to trust the numbers.

[03:52] Marcus: Yep, we'll attach logs. Note that our tail latency improvement came with a small throughput cost - tokens/sec dropped to ~2100 in that config. It's a classic latency vs throughput tradeoff.

[04:20] Sofia: Is there an option to keep throughput high and still get low p99?

[04:24] Marcus: Two options: (1) Dedicated nodes where you have reserved capacity and less noisy neighbors - that usually stabilizes p99 without aggressive batching; (2) Adaptive batching policy where we cap concurrency per worker and route latency-sensitive requests to lower-batch paths. Both cost different amounts.

[05:05] Avery: Also quantization. You were testing 4-bit quant, right?

[05:10] Sofia: We tested 4-bit on Baseline and saw throughput gains but occasional quality regressions.

[05:16] Marcus: On Redwood we tested quant-4 and quant-8. Quant-4 gave ~1.4x throughput vs quant-8, but p99 instability increased ~15% on some prompt types. For production, we recommend quant-8 for now until we do targeted evals on your prompt set; quant-4 could be used for non-critical high-volume endpoints.

[06:02] Ethan: What's the impact of multi-turn KV cache? Our prompts have long context and many repeated prefixes.

[06:09] Marcus: Significant. With prefix KV caching enabled and a warm cache, token generation CPU/GPU work drops dramatically for repeated contexts - effectively reduces work per request and smooths latency. In our warm-cache run the p99 dropped from 610ms to 380ms as I said. The baseline provider doesn't do prefix caching as aggressively, which explains some of the delta.

[06:50] Priya: Any risks with cache warmup on production? Miss rates?

[06:55] Marcus: Miss rates depend on prompt diversity. We saw ~65% hit rate on your sample prompt mix during the 1h trace you sent. If you can give a 24h sample we can estimate steady state. There's also cache size settings and eviction policy we can tune. We'll recommend conservative TTLs to avoid stale outputs.

[07:30] Leah (Redwood CSM): I'll note that and ask for the 24h sample in the action items.

[07:40] Sofia: About the Dedicated option - can you summarize cost vs benefit?

[07:45] Avery: Sure. Dedicated gives reserved GPUs, predictable throughput, and avoids multi-tenant noisy neighbor issues. It also allows sizing (e.g., 4xA10 or 2xH100) and custom kernel selection. Pricing is on a reserved monthly basis; we'll send a tailored quote. For p99-sensitive workloads with steady traffic, Dedicated often yields better total cost of ownership.

[08:25] Ethan: We are currently leaning toward Hosted for quick go-live, but Dedicated if p99 can't be stabilized.

[08:33] Marcus: Makes sense. We also have routing fallbacks - you can pin critical traffic to lower-batch, lower-latency paths while sending bulk traffic to higher-throughput lanes. That hybrid routing keeps latency SLOs while optimizing cost.

[09:00] Sofia: For the runs you did, what's the request concurrency and sequence lengths? The p99 is sensitive to long sequences.

[09:06] Marcus: Good question. Our runs used the prompt mix you gave: median length 120 tokens, 95th percentile 420 tokens. Concurrency simulated 60 concurrent active users with Poisson arrivals - same as your baseline test harness. We also ran a 200-concurrency stress test which showed p99 spikes that can be mitigated by Dedicated or adaptive routing.

[09:55] Priya: Security due diligence - we need SOC2 and encryption at rest assurances to move forward on Dedicated.

[10:01] Avery: We'll send SOC2 Type II and encryption/KMS docs. For Private/VPC options we can support customer-managed KMS and audit logs. I'll include links in the follow-up email.

[10:18] Ravi: On telemetry - can we get token-level cost breakdowns in the console? We want to map tokens to feature routes.

[10:24] Leah: Yes, Redwood Console exposes per-route token breakdowns, latency histograms, and tracing hooks. We'll set up a demo workspace with your routes so you can explore.

[10:35] Sofia: Back to the numbers, can you walk through the spreadsheet cells that show p95 and p99 for the five runs?

[10:42] Marcus: Sure. Sheet run A: hosted default (no cache) p95 210ms / p99 610ms / throughput 2300 tps. Run B: hosted + kv warm p95 220ms / p99 380ms / throughput 2100. Run C: hosted + conservative batch_delay p95 205ms / p99 400ms / throughput 2200. Run D: quant-4 aggressive p95 180ms / p99 700ms / throughput 3200 (but quality issues on some prompts). Run E: dedicated small cluster sim simulated p95 200ms / p99 320ms / throughput 2400. Baseline numbers (as provided by Greenline): p95 240ms / p99 430ms / throughput 1800.

[12:05] Ethan: The quant-4 p99 spike worries me, good to see quality issues. We can't accept regression for critical flows.

[12:12] Marcus: Agreed, that's why we recommend quant-8 default. We can run targeted evals to identify which prompts break under quant-4 and isolate them.

[12:30] Sofia: About reproducibility - can you provide Dockerized runners or the exact harness you used? Our infra team wants to reproduce.

[12:38] Marcus: Yes, we'll share the benchmark harness and the exact command line flags (batch_size, max_batch_delay_ms, cache settings, concurrency script). We'll also include raw logs and sampled traces.

[13:00] Priya: One more ops question - If we go Dedicated, how does scaling work? Autoscale? Warmup times?

[13:07] Avery: Dedicated supports autoscaling policies and warm pool options. Typically spin-up for extra capacity is a few minutes depending on instance type; for latency-sensitive flows teams keep a minimum reserved pool to avoid spin-up. We can help size that.

[13:34] Ravi: Are there any limits around KV cache memory or eviction that could blow up costs?

[13:40] Marcus: Cache memory is configurable per node. Costs come from memory footprint on GPUs; we can size cache to your hit-rate targets. We'll show tradeoff curves in the spreadsheet.

[14:05] Sofia: Ok, let's talk acceptance criteria for the pilot. We need p95 < 250ms and p99 < 450ms on the production prompt mix for a continuous 24h run at target concurrency. If Redwood can demonstrate that on Dedicated or Hosted+cache with routing, we greenlight production pilot.

[14:30] Avery: Understood. We'll plan a 24h run on Dedicated nodes (or hosted with pinned capacity) and provide results.

[14:40] Leah: I'll coordinate scheduling and permissions.

[14:45] Marcus: For the 24h run we will: 1) ask for 24h sample of traffic, 2) provision a Dedicated test cluster for a day or run in hosted with pinned capacity, 3) execute runs with KV cache warm, various batching settings, and quantization profiles, 4) share raw logs + dashboard links.

[15:10] Sofia: That sounds good. Action items?

[15:14] Avery: Recap. Avery: send updated benchmark sheet + SOC2/ISO docs + Dedicated pricing by 2025-05-10. Marcus: run p99 KV-cache-enabled test and attach logs by 2025-05-12. Priya: confirm dates for on-site Dedicated run by 2025-05-12. Sofia: provide 24h traffic sample and prompt mix by 2025-05-09. Leah: set up console demo workspace and invite Greenline users by 2025-05-09.

[15:40] Ethan: One last question - fallback behavior if a node is saturated? We need no total outage.

[15:46] Marcus: We have automatic fallback policies: route to alternate region, route to a higher-cost low-latency lane, or queue with explicit SLA. We'll document recommended fallback for your architecture.

[16:05] Priya: Great. That covers my concerns for now.

[16:10] Sofia: Thanks all.

[16:12] Avery: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the artifacts.

[54:30] [meeting end - informal chatter and wrap up]

Notes on transcription quality: some product names transcribed as r-model or redwood-serve, BaselineCloudAI sometimes mis-typoed.

References: "benchmark_spreadsheet_v3.xlsx" (shared link), SOC2 and encryption docs (links to be sent).

Recorded next steps repeated at end: send pricing/security, run KV warm p99, schedule on-site Dedicated run")
